instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and set a rimmed baking sheet on the counter.
Halve the cherry tomatoes. Thinly slice the garlic. Cut the lemon into 8 thin slices. Drain the capers.
Pat the fish dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Lay the 4 sheets of parchment on the counter. Put a fillet in the middle of each, then top each with 2 lemon slices and 2 thyme sprigs.
Pile the tomatoes, olives, capers and garlic around and over the fish, dividing them evenly.
Spoon 1 tbsp of the wine and 1 tbsp of the oil over each fillet.
Bring the long edges of each parchment sheet together over the fish and fold them down twice. Twist and fold the two ends under to seal the packet tightly. Transfer the packets to the baking sheet.

Bake for 12 to 14 minutes, until the packets puff up. You're cooking the fish to 145°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check one through the paper. No thermometer? Open one packet. The fish should be opaque and flake easily with a fork.
Transfer each packet to a plate and open it at the table. Serve with boiled potatoes or rice, and spoon the juices in the packet over the fish.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
method_notes: Foodcraft's Pesce al Cartoccio (4.4 from 48) bakes whole sea bream with tomatoes, olives, capers, lemon, garlic, thyme, wine and oil in sealed paper at 200°C, and gives no bake time. It is changed here to white fish fillets so it fits a weeknight (cod, halibut or sea bass). The 425°F and 12 to 14 minutes come from a fillet-in-parchment recipe by Sandra Valvassori (5 from 1 vote, labelled French). Olives are pitted and the wine is cut to a spoonful per packet. About 30 minutes in all.
